 152: \(s^{-2r}\) quadratic tensor coefficient for two arbitrary inputs matching
 153: all lower moments, under the endpoint \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\)-moment, and proves
 154: that no smaller absolute-moment exponent works uniformly over the complete
 155: moment class: for \(d+\alpha>2r\) this is analytic uniform sharpness on
 156: pairs with a finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor, whereas for
 157: \(d+\alpha\le2r\) the value \(p_{r,\alpha,d}=r\) is only coefficient-domain
 158: minimality below order \(r\).
 159: 
 160: The exact law-by-law interface also holds at every order.  Under only finite
 161: \(r\)th moments and matching below \(r\),
 162: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition} retains
 163: the common lower-order Taylor jet and each law's unexpanded exterior
 164: translate mixture in positive densities \(k_{r,s}^\nu,k_{r,s}^\eta\).  It
 165: proves
 166: \[
 167:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 168:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
 169:  +D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
 170: \]
 171: \input{sec_introduction_proxy_robustness}
 172: Thus the universal coefficient is attained exactly when the nonnegative
 173: tail-proxy entropy is \(o(s^{-2r})\).  At covariance order against the
 174: point mass at the common mean this reduces, up to \(o(s^{-4})\), to the
 175: one-sided raw-tail \(\Phi\)-energy in
 176: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.  When
 177: \(d+\alpha\le4\), finite covariance forces that energy to vanish at the
 178: required scale; when \(d+\alpha>4\), it is a genuinely additional
 179: law-by-law condition.  The infinite
 180: critical-moment boundary is genuinely different: Theorem
 181: \ref{thm:critical-vague-tail-nonidentifiability} constructs two laws with the
 182: same smooth multivariate regularly varying tail data and the same covariance,
 183: one attaining the covariance coefficient and the other having unbounded
 184: scaled entropy along a subsequence.
 185: Theorem~\ref{thm:covariance-proxy-defect-decomposition} gives an
 186: asymptotically exact
 187: finite-covariance characterization of this distinction.  If
 188: \(k_{\Sigma,t}\) denotes the positive Poisson density obtained by adjoining
 189: the normalized quadratic mode \(t^{-2}b_\Sigma\) to the matched reference,
 190: then
 191: \[
 192:  t^4H_d(t)=\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)
 193:  +t^4D_{\rm KL}(h_t\|k_{\Sigma,t})+o(1).
 194: \]
 195: Thus attainment of the covariance coefficient is equivalent to the
 196: vanishing of the complete nonlinear proxy defect.  This statement requires
 197: only finite covariance and does not impose a density or tail regularity on
 198: the original law.
 199: The leading multidimensional covariance formula is deliberately read through
 200: this analytic route.  Finite covariance alone determines the bounded quadratic
 201: mode \(b_\Sigma\) and the algebraic number \(\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)\), but it
 202: does not by itself make \(\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)\) the coefficient of
 203: \eqref{eq:intro-main-functional}.  It becomes the leading KL coefficient only
 204: after a quotient/existence bridge is in force, for example the
 205: \((\mathrm{MPJ}_{d,L})+(\mathrm{EX}_{d,L})\) package supplied here by
 206: finite \(L\)-moment with \(L\ge d+1\), or the separate second-order quotient
 207: criterion stated in Section~\ref{sec:entropy-asymptotics}.
 208: 
 209: The nearest prior work for the heavy-tailed density estimates is
 210: Ishige--Kawakami--Michihisa
 211: \cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017} and the refined follow-up
 212: \cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}.  For every
 213: \(0<\alpha<2\) and weighted moment order \(K\ge0\), those works subtract
 214: moment-weighted derivatives of the stable heat kernel and prove scaled
 215: \(L^q\) and weighted \(L^1\) remainder decay for the resulting density
 216: expansion, including inhomogeneous and nonlinear refinements.  They do not
 217: control the matched density quotient in
 218: \(L^{q_{\alpha,d}}(p_1^{(\alpha,d)}\dd y)\) or transfer that critical
 219: estimate through relative entropy; those are the steps that produce
 220: \(p_{\alpha,d}\) here.  They also do not retain the unexpanded translate
 221: mixture beyond the smoothing scale as the nonlinear entropy energy in
 222: Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition}.
 223: In contrast, Chen--Niles-Weed give the direct Gaussian KL precedent
 224: \eqref{eq:intro-chen-niles-weed-kl}; the present comparison with the
 225: fractional-diffusion literature is only a comparison of the heavy-tailed
 226: analytic inputs and does not erase that priority.
 227: 
 228: The novelty claim is correspondingly narrow.  Arbitrary-order Gaussian
 229: first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotics are prior work, and all-order
 230: stable/fractional density expansions are prior work.  To the best of our
 231: knowledge, what is new here is the nonnegative law-by-law decomposition under
 232: stable smoothing into the universal tensor coefficient and the KL divergence
 233: of two explicit positive tail-jet proxies, under only finite \(r\)-th
 234: moments, with proxy vanishing as an exact coefficient-attainment criterion.
 235: \input{sec_introduction_proxy_scope}
 236: 
 237: \ifdefined\JFAArticleMain
 238: The full domain-closure motivation and comparison with the general
 239: two-solution Bregman calculus are in \path{sec_introduction.tex}, the
 240: paragraphs preceding ``Theorems,'' collected by
 241: \path{supplement_relocated_support.tex}.
 242: \else
 243: The third theorem is a domain-and-endpoint result for the standard
 244: simultaneous-semigroup relative-entropy calculus.  For a symmetric jump
 245: generator
 246: \[
 247: (L_Jf)(x)=\int\{f(y)-f(x)\}J(x,y)\,\dd y,
 248: \qquad J(x,y)=J(y,x),
 249: \]
 250: and sufficiently regular positive solutions
 251: \(\partial_t h_t=L_Jh_t\), \(\partial_t g_t=L_Jg_t\), set
 252: \(u_t=h_t/g_t\).  The general generator identity is
 253: \begin{equation}\label{eq:intro-general-two-solution-generator-identity}
 254: -\frac{\dd}{\dd t}D_{\rm KL}(h_t\|g_t)
 255: =\frac12\iint J(x,y)
 501: \]
 502: Equivalently,
 503: \[
 504: \mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)
 505: =\frac12\int_{\RR^d}b_\Sigma(y)^2\,\Omega_d(\dd y),
 506: \quad
 507: b_\Sigma(y)=
 508: \frac{d+1}{2}\left(
 509: -\frac{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma}{1+|y|^2}
 510: +\frac{(d+3)y^{\mathsf T}\Sigma y}{(1+|y|^2)^2}
 511: \right).
 512: \]
 513: Separately, let \(0<\alpha<2\) and let
 514: \(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(x)=s^{-d}p_1^{(\alpha,d)}(x/s)\) be any isotropic
 515: strictly \(\alpha\)-stable kernel.  If
 516: \[
 517:  \EE|X_c|^{p_{\alpha,d}}<\infty,
 518:  \qquad
 519:  p_{\alpha,d}=\max\left\{2,
 520:  \frac{4(d+\alpha)}{d+\alpha+4}\right\},
 521: \]
 522: then
 523: \[
 524:  D_{\rm KL}\!\left(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\,\middle\|\,
 525:  p_s^{(\alpha,d)}(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma)\right)
 526:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d}(\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),
 527: \]
 528: with \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d}\) defined in
 529: \eqref{eq:stable-leading-covariance-functional}.  The exponent is optimal
 530: as a uniform sufficient finite-moment hypothesis, including its endpoint;
 531: no smaller absolute-moment exponent works uniformly over its full moment
 532: class.
 533: 
 534: More generally, let \(r\ge1\), let \(\nu,\eta\) be probability laws on
 535: \(\RR^d\), and assume that their tensor moments agree below order \(r\),
 536: their order-\(r\) tensor difference \(\Delta_r\) is nonzero, and both have
 537: finite \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\)th absolute moments, where
 538: \[
 539:  q_{r,\alpha,d}=\min\left\{2,1+\frac{2r}{d+\alpha}\right\},
 540:  \qquad
 541:  p_{r,\alpha,d}=\frac{2r}{q_{r,\alpha,d}}.
 542: \]
 543: Then
 544: \[
 545:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 546:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}+o(s^{-2r}),
 547: \]
 548: where \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}\) is the strictly positive quadratic
 549: functional in \eqref{eq:all-order-stable-leading-functional}.  The endpoint
 550: \(p_{r,\alpha,d}\) is optimal as a uniform sufficient absolute-moment
 551: exponent.  This extends the Gaussian theorem of Chen--Niles-Weed from
 552: sub-Gaussian inputs to heavy-tailed stable kernels with the critical complete
 553: moment assumption.  For \(d+\alpha>2r\), sharpness below the endpoint holds even
 554: among pairs with finite nonzero order-\(r\) tensor difference; below \(r\)
 555: the obstruction is instead that the coefficient need not be defined.  In
 556: dimension one, Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-gaussian-quadrature-threshold}
 557: converts this statement into a finite/infinite \(2n\)th-moment equivalence
 558: for Gaussian quadrature under every symmetric stable index.
 559: 
 560: Under the weaker, law-specific hypothesis
 561: \(\int|x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty\), define the positive tail-jet proxy
 562: densities \(k_{r,s}^\nu,k_{r,s}^\eta\) by
 563: \eqref{eq:arbitrary-tail-proxy-quotients}.  Then
 564: \[
 565:  D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 566:  =\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
 567:  +D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)+o(s^{-2r}),
 568: \]
 569: and therefore
 570: \[
 571:  s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\nu\|p_s^{(\alpha,d)}*\eta)
 572:  \to\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}(\Delta_r)
 573:  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 574:  s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(k_{r,s}^\nu\|k_{r,s}^\eta)\to0.
 575: \]
 576: This arbitrary-order criterion assumes no regular variation, absolute
 577: continuity, or moment above order \(r\).  Its order-two specialization
 578: recovers the one-sided raw-tail energy displayed above.
 579: \end{maintheorem}

from pathlib import Path
import re
import unittest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
INPUT_RE = re.compile(r"\\input\{([^}]+)\}")


def read_tex_source(path: Path) -> str:
    """Read a TeX source together with any local input wrappers."""

    source = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def expand(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        child = ROOT / match.group(1)
        if child.suffix == "":
            child = child.with_suffix(".tex")
        return read_tex_source(child)

    return INPUT_RE.sub(expand, source)

+\subsection*{The positive tail-jet mechanism for an abstract kernel}
+
+We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  Fix
+an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive probability density
+\(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet admissible of order \(r\)}
+if the following three conditions hold.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
+\]
+\item The top normalized derivative has the quotient translation modulus
+\[
+ \omega_{p,r}(t):=
+ \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
+                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
+ \qquad 0<t\le1,
+\]
+finite for \(0<t\le1\) and satisfying
+\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
+\item The translate entropy is finite and, for some \(C_{p,r}<\infty\),
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z):=
+ D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)
+ \le C_{p,r}(1+|z|^r),\qquad z\in\RR^d.
+\]
+\end{enumerate}
+Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
+\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
+\]
+For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
+\[
+ B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
+\]
+
+\begin{unnumberedtheorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
+Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
+probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
+\[
+ m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
+ \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
+\[
+ \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
+ V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
+ \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
+\begin{align*}
+ C_{p,r-1,s}
+ &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
+  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
+ A_{p,s}^\lambda
+ &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
+\end{align*}
+The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
+\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
+\[
+ k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
+\]
+are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
+\]
+is well defined.  If
+\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
+\[
+ B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
+ \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
+ \qquad
+ \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
+\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedtheorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We give every kernel-dependent step.  Let
+\[
+ \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
+ \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
+\]
+Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
+ +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
+ \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
+\]
+It also gives \(D^rp\in L^1\).  Consequently ordinary translation
+continuity in \(L^1\), the integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply
+that, for \(|z|\le1\),
+\begin{align*}
+ &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\\
+ &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
+\end{align*}
+where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
+zero.  Indeed, after subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial, the
+uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
+\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\[
+ |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
+ \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
+\]
+which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  This proves the required local Taylor statement
+without a derivative of order \(r+1\).
+
+Define the actual quotient
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
+the moments gives
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda
+ =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
+ +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+For completeness, after multiplication by \(s^r\) the interior Taylor
+remainder is dominated by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every
+discarded exterior mode satisfies
+\[
+ s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
+ \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad j\le r.
+\]
+The same tail-moment estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Translation preserves mass.  Hence \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\), and integration of
+the distributional derivatives of the integrable density \(p\) gives
+\(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass one,
+and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This is both proxy normalization and proxy positivity; no tail comparison is
+used.
+
+We next verify entropy finiteness.  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
+relative entropy and \textup{(K3)} give, for the normalized exterior mixture
+quotient \(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
+ \le\frac{C_{p,r}}{\tau_s^\lambda}
+ \int_{|x|>s}\{1+|x/s|^r\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The elementary inequalities
+\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
+\[
+ (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
+ \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
+\]
+then show
+\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
+The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
+common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.
+
+It remains to identify the quadratic term.  Condition \textup{(K1)} at
+order one says \(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty=L<\infty\).  Thus
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
+\]
+uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
+their common jet cancels, so
+\begin{align*}
+ \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
+ &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
+      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
+ \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
+ &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{align*}
+All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are now
+satisfied with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder
+calculation gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
+       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
+\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving the decomposition.
+
+Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
+vanishes, then
+\[
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p=0
+\]
+almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
+\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
+polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
+nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
+is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
+Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
+\end{proof}
+
+The hypotheses above are arranged by proof function, not by tail class.
+Condition \textup{(K1)} defines and bounds the retained modes, makes their
+integrals vanish, and supplies the logarithmic-gradient lower bound.
+Condition \textup{(K2)} is exactly the uniform little-\(o\) Taylor remainder;
+the \(L^1\) counterpart is automatic because \textup{(K1)} puts \(D^rp\) in
+\(L^1\).  Condition \textup{(K3)} is used only to make the retained-tail and
+proxy entropies finite.  Neither decay, regular variation, a semigroup law,
+radial symmetry, nor isotropy is assumed.  Isotropy merely adds orthogonal
+invariance of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\).
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Verified kernels and the Gaussian boundary]
+For every order \(r\ge1\), the abstract theorem applies to each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), to the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and to every multivariate Student kernel
+\[
+ p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
+\]
+For the stable density, the specialization is exactly Theorem
+\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, with identical
+proxies, energy, and quadratic form.  The standard Gaussian density is not
+tail-jet admissible: \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)} fail, and the additive
+retained common jet need not be positive.  Thus the abstract theorem makes no
+Gaussian claim.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+\emph{Isotropic stable kernels.}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} gives, with
+\(\beta=d+\alpha\),
+\[
+ p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
+ (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
+\]
+This proves \textup{(K1)}.  For \(|h|\le1\), the mean-value theorem, the
+bound at order \(r+1\), and
+\(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
+\[
+ \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
+ \le C|h|,qquad |\gamma|=r,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+so \textup{(K2)} holds.  The two-sided density estimate also gives
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z)\le C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|),
+\]
+which is \textup{(K3)} for every \(r\ge1\).  The abstract definitions of
+\(F_y^p\), \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\), \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are respectively the definitions used in
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Hence
+that theorem is precisely this specialization, not a weakened consequence.
+
+\emph{Poisson kernel.}
+At unit height the Poisson kernel on \(\RR^d\) is
+\[
+ P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}.
+\]
+The derivative calculation in the next paragraph with \(\beta=d+1\)
+verifies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}, while the displayed entropy bound
+there verifies \textup{(K3)}.  Its spatial dilates are exactly
+\(P_s^{(d)}(x)=c_ds(s^2+|x|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  This is also the
+\(\alpha=1\) stable member, but the rational formula proves membership
+directly, without stable-density estimates.
+
+\emph{Multivariate Student kernels.}
+Let \(\beta>d\).  Repeated differentiation shows that every normalized
+derivative \(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of
+terms
+\[
+ c_{\gamma,k}\,
+ \frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^{k}},
+ \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
+\]
+and is therefore bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together
+with
+\[
+ \frac{p_{\beta,d}(y-th)}{p_{\beta,d}(y)}\le C_{\beta,d},
+ \qquad |h|\le1,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+and the mean-value theorem gives \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \sqrt{1+|w+z|^2}
+ \le\sqrt{1+|w|^2}+|z|
+ \le(1+|z|)\sqrt{1+|w|^2},
+\]
+so
+\[
+ \log\frac{p_{\beta,d}(w)}{p_{\beta,d}(w+z)}
+ \le\beta\log(1+|z|).
+\]
+Integration against \(p_{\beta,d}(w)\dd w\) proves \textup{(K3)}.
+This supplies a nonstable polynomial-tail family for every \(\beta>d\);
+only the value \(\beta=d+1\) is the Poisson/stable case.
+
+\emph{Gaussian obstruction.}
+For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
+\[
+ \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
+ \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
+\]
+so the normalized derivatives are unbounded and \textup{(K1)} fails at its
+first derivative.  The translate quotient
+\[
+ F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
+\]
+has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\); hence the uniform lower bound for the
+actual quotients used by the two-background expansion is unavailable.  The
+proxy failure is already explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
+\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
+\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
+They have the same moments below order two.  For \(s>|m|+a\) the retained
+tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); therefore both
+prescribed proxies equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a half-line.
+Thus proxy positivity, the background lower bound, and the bounded cubic
+remainder all fail at the same additive-jet step.  Gaussian translate entropy
+itself is not the obstruction when \(r\ge2\), since
+\(\mathsf H_g(z)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments can and do prove
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input hypotheses,
+as recalled above, but they are not instances of this positive additive
+tail-proxy mechanism.
+\end{proof}

+The theorem is a specialization of the unnumbered abstract kernel theorem
+that precedes it.  For a strictly positive density \(p\), the proof uses only
+bounded normalized derivatives through order \(r\), uniform
+translation-continuity of the normalized order-\(r\) derivative, and an
+order-\(r\) bound on the entropy of a translate of \(p\).  These conditions

+for every multivariate Student density \(c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2}\),

+condition: its normalized derivatives are Hermite polynomials, and an
+additive common jet need not remain positive.  Thus the Gaussian
+first-unmatched-moment theorem recalled above uses a different weighted
+Hermite mechanism; it is not presented as a member of the positive
+tail-proxy theorem.

+\subsection*{The positive tail-jet mechanism for an abstract kernel}
+
+We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  Fix
+an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive probability density
+\(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet admissible of order \(r\)}
+if the following three conditions hold.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
+\]
+\item The top normalized derivative has the quotient translation modulus
+\[
+ \omega_{p,r}(t):=
+ \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
+                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
+ \qquad 0<t\le1,
+\]
+finite for \(0<t\le1\) and satisfying
+\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
+\item The translate entropy is finite and, for some \(C_{p,r}<\infty\),
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z):=
+ D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)
+ \le C_{p,r}(1+|z|^r),\qquad z\in\RR^d.
+\]
+\end{enumerate}
+Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
+\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
+\]
+For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
+\[
+ B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
+\]
+
+\begin{unnumberedtheorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
+Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
+probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
+\[
+ m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
+ \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
+\[
+ \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
+ V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
+ \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
+\begin{align*}
+ C_{p,r-1,s}
+ &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
+  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
+ A_{p,s}^\lambda
+ &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
+\end{align*}
+The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
+\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
+\[
+ k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
+\]
+are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
+\]
+is well defined.  If
+\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
+\[
+ B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
+ \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
+ \qquad
+ \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
+\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedtheorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We give every kernel-dependent step.  Let
+\[
+ \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
+ \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
+\]
+Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
+ +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
+ \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
+\]
+It also gives \(D^rp\in L^1\).  Consequently ordinary translation
+continuity in \(L^1\), the integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply
+that, for \(|z|\le1\),
+\begin{align*}
+ &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\\
+ &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
+\end{align*}
+where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
+zero.  Indeed, after subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial, the
+uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
+\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\[
+ |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
+ \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
+\]
+which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  This proves the required local Taylor statement
+without a derivative of order \(r+1\).
+
+Define the actual quotient
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
+the moments gives
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda
+ =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
+ +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+For completeness, after multiplication by \(s^r\) the interior Taylor
+remainder is dominated by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every
+discarded exterior mode satisfies
+\[
+ s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
+ \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad j\le r.
+\]
+The same tail-moment estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Translation preserves mass.  Hence \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\), and integration of
+the distributional derivatives of the integrable density \(p\) gives
+\(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass one,
+and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This is both proxy normalization and proxy positivity; no tail comparison is
+used.
+
+We next verify entropy finiteness.  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
+relative entropy and \textup{(K3)} give, for the normalized exterior mixture
+quotient \(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
+ \le\frac{C_{p,r}}{\tau_s^\lambda}
+ \int_{|x|>s}\{1+|x/s|^r\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The elementary inequalities
+\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
+\[
+ (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
+ \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
+\]
+then show
+\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
+The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
+common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.
+
+It remains to identify the quadratic term.  Condition \textup{(K1)} at
+order one says \(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty=L<\infty\).  Thus
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
+\]
+uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
+their common jet cancels, so
+\begin{align*}
+ \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
+ &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
+      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
+ \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
+ &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{align*}
+All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are now
+satisfied with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder
+calculation gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
+       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
+\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving the decomposition.
+
+Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
+vanishes, then
+\[
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p=0
+\]
+almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
+\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
+polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
+nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
+is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
+Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
+\end{proof}
+
+The hypotheses above are arranged by proof function, not by tail class.
+Condition \textup{(K1)} defines and bounds the retained modes, makes their
+integrals vanish, and supplies the logarithmic-gradient lower bound.
+Condition \textup{(K2)} is exactly the uniform little-\(o\) Taylor remainder;
+the \(L^1\) counterpart is automatic because \textup{(K1)} puts \(D^rp\) in
+\(L^1\).  Condition \textup{(K3)} is used only to make the retained-tail and
+proxy entropies finite.  Neither decay, regular variation, a semigroup law,
+radial symmetry, nor isotropy is assumed.  Isotropy merely adds orthogonal
+invariance of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\).
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Verified kernels and the Gaussian boundary]
+For every order \(r\ge1\), the abstract theorem applies to each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), to the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and to every multivariate Student kernel
+\[
+ p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
+\]
+For the stable density, the specialization is exactly Theorem
+\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, with identical
+proxies, energy, and quadratic form.  The standard Gaussian density is not
+tail-jet admissible: \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)} fail, and the additive
+retained common jet need not be positive.  Thus the abstract theorem makes no
+Gaussian claim.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+\emph{Isotropic stable kernels.}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} gives, with
+\(\beta=d+\alpha\),
+\[
+ p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
+ (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
+\]
+This proves \textup{(K1)}.  For \(|h|\le1\), the mean-value theorem, the
+bound at order \(r+1\), and
+\(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
+\[
+ \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
+ \le C|h|,qquad |\gamma|=r,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+so \textup{(K2)} holds.  The two-sided density estimate also gives
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z)\le C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|),
+\]
+which is \textup{(K3)} for every \(r\ge1\).  The abstract definitions of
+\(F_y^p\), \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\), \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are respectively the definitions used in
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Hence
+that theorem is precisely this specialization, not a weakened consequence.
+
+\emph{Poisson kernel.}
+At unit height the Poisson kernel on \(\RR^d\) is
+\[
+ P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}.
+\]
+The derivative calculation in the next paragraph with \(\beta=d+1\)
+verifies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}, while the displayed entropy bound
+there verifies \textup{(K3)}.  Its spatial dilates are exactly
+\(P_s^{(d)}(x)=c_ds(s^2+|x|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  This is also the
+\(\alpha=1\) stable member, but the rational formula proves membership
+directly, without stable-density estimates.
+
+\emph{Multivariate Student kernels.}
+Let \(\beta>d\).  Repeated differentiation shows that every normalized
+derivative \(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of
+terms
+\[
+ c_{\gamma,k}\,
+ \frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^{k}},
+ \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
+\]
+and is therefore bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together
+with
+\[
+ \frac{p_{\beta,d}(y-th)}{p_{\beta,d}(y)}\le C_{\beta,d},
+ \qquad |h|\le1,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+and the mean-value theorem gives \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \sqrt{1+|w+z|^2}
+ \le\sqrt{1+|w|^2}+|z|
+ \le(1+|z|)\sqrt{1+|w|^2},
+\]
+so
+\[
+ \log\frac{p_{\beta,d}(w)}{p_{\beta,d}(w+z)}
+ \le\beta\log(1+|z|).
+\]
+Integration against \(p_{\beta,d}(w)\dd w\) proves \textup{(K3)}.
+This supplies a nonstable polynomial-tail family for every \(\beta>d\);
+only the value \(\beta=d+1\) is the Poisson/stable case.
+
+\emph{Gaussian obstruction.}
+For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
+\[
+ \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
+ \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
+\]
+so the normalized derivatives are unbounded and \textup{(K1)} fails at its
+first derivative.  The translate quotient
+\[
+ F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
+\]
+has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\); hence the uniform lower bound for the
+actual quotients used by the two-background expansion is unavailable.  The
+proxy failure is already explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
+\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
+\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
+They have the same moments below order two.  For \(s>|m|+a\) the retained
+tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); therefore both
+prescribed proxies equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a half-line.
+Thus proxy positivity, the background lower bound, and the bounded cubic
+remainder all fail at the same additive-jet step.  Gaussian translate entropy
+itself is not the obstruction when \(r\ge2\), since
+\(\mathsf H_g(z)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments can and do prove
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input hypotheses,
+as recalled above, but they are not instances of this positive additive
+tail-proxy mechanism.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection*{The positive tail-jet mechanism for an abstract kernel}
+
+We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  Fix
+an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive probability density
+\(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet admissible of order \(r\)}
+if the following three conditions hold.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
+\]
+\item The top normalized derivative has the quotient translation modulus
+\[
+ \omega_{p,r}(t):=
+ \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
+                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
+ \qquad 0<t\le1,
+\]
+finite for \(0<t\le1\) and satisfying
+\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
+\item The translate entropy is finite and, for some \(C_{p,r}<\infty\),
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z):=
+ D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)
+ \le C_{p,r}(1+|z|^r),\qquad z\in\RR^d.
+\]
+\end{enumerate}
+Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
+\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
+\]
+For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
+\[
+ B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
+\]
+
+\begin{unnumberedtheorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
+Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
+probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
+\[
+ m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
+ \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
+\[
+ \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
+ V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
+ \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
+\begin{align*}
+ C_{p,r-1,s}
+ &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
+  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
+ A_{p,s}^\lambda
+ &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
+\end{align*}
+The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
+\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
+\[
+ k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
+\]
+are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
+\]
+is well defined.  If
+\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
+\[
+ B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
+ \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
+ \qquad
+ \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
+\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedtheorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We give every kernel-dependent step.  Let
+\[
+ \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
+ \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
+\]
+Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
+ +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
+ \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
+\]
+It also gives \(D^rp\in L^1\).  Consequently ordinary translation
+continuity in \(L^1\), the integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply
+that, for \(|z|\le1\),
+\begin{align*}
+ &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\\
+ &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
+\end{align*}
+where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
+zero.  Indeed, after subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial, the
+uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
+\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\[
+ |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
+ \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
+\]
+which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  This proves the required local Taylor statement
+without a derivative of order \(r+1\).
+
+Define the actual quotient
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
+the moments gives
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda
+ =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
+ +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+For completeness, after multiplication by \(s^r\) the interior Taylor
+remainder is dominated by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every
+discarded exterior mode satisfies
+\[
+ s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
+ \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad j\le r.
+\]
+The same tail-moment estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Translation preserves mass.  Hence \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\), and integration of
+the distributional derivatives of the integrable density \(p\) gives
+\(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass one,
+and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This is both proxy normalization and proxy positivity; no tail comparison is
+used.
+
+We next verify entropy finiteness.  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
+relative entropy and \textup{(K3)} give, for the normalized exterior mixture
+quotient \(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
+ \le\frac{C_{p,r}}{\tau_s^\lambda}
+ \int_{|x|>s}\{1+|x/s|^r\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The elementary inequalities
+\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
+\[
+ (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
+ \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
+\]
+then show
+\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
+The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
+common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.
+
+It remains to identify the quadratic term.  Condition \textup{(K1)} at
+order one says \(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty=L<\infty\).  Thus
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
+\]
+uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
+their common jet cancels, so
+\begin{align*}
+ \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
+ &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
+      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
+ \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
+ &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{align*}
+All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are now
+satisfied with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder
+calculation gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
+       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
+\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving the decomposition.
+
+Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
+vanishes, then
+\[
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p=0
+\]
+almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
+\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
+polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
+nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
+is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
+Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
+\end{proof}
+
+The hypotheses above are arranged by proof function, not by tail class.
+Condition \textup{(K1)} defines and bounds the retained modes, makes their
+integrals vanish, and supplies the logarithmic-gradient lower bound.
+Condition \textup{(K2)} is exactly the uniform little-\(o\) Taylor remainder;
+the \(L^1\) counterpart is automatic because \textup{(K1)} puts \(D^rp\) in
+\(L^1\).  Condition \textup{(K3)} is used only to make the retained-tail and
+proxy entropies finite.  Neither decay, regular variation, a semigroup law,
+radial symmetry, nor isotropy is assumed.  Isotropy merely adds orthogonal
+invariance of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\).
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Verified kernels and the Gaussian boundary]
+For every order \(r\ge1\), the abstract theorem applies to each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), to the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and to every multivariate Student kernel
+\[
+ p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
+\]
+For the stable density, the specialization is exactly Theorem
+\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, with identical
+proxies, energy, and quadratic form.  The standard Gaussian density is not
+tail-jet admissible: \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)} fail, and the additive
+retained common jet need not be positive.  Thus the abstract theorem makes no
+Gaussian claim.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+\emph{Isotropic stable kernels.}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} gives, with
+\(\beta=d+\alpha\),
+\[
+ p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
+ (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
+\]
+This proves \textup{(K1)}.  For \(|h|\le1\), the mean-value theorem, the
+bound at order \(r+1\), and
+\(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
+\[
+ \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
+ \le C|h|,qquad |\gamma|=r,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+so \textup{(K2)} holds.  The two-sided density estimate also gives
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z)\le C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|),
+\]
+which is \textup{(K3)} for every \(r\ge1\).  The abstract definitions of
+\(F_y^p\), \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\), \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are respectively the definitions used in
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Hence
+that theorem is precisely this specialization, not a weakened consequence.
+
+\emph{Poisson kernel.}
+At unit height the Poisson kernel on \(\RR^d\) is
+\[
+ P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}.
+\]
+The derivative calculation in the next paragraph with \(\beta=d+1\)
+verifies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}, while the displayed entropy bound
+there verifies \textup{(K3)}.  Its spatial dilates are exactly
+\(P_s^{(d)}(x)=c_ds(s^2+|x|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  This is also the
+\(\alpha=1\) stable member, but the rational formula proves membership
+directly, without stable-density estimates.
+
+\emph{Multivariate Student kernels.}
+Let \(\beta>d\).  Repeated differentiation shows that every normalized
+derivative \(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of
+terms
+\[
+ c_{\gamma,k}\,
+ \frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^{k}},
+ \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
+\]
+and is therefore bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together
+with
+\[
+ \frac{p_{\beta,d}(y-th)}{p_{\beta,d}(y)}\le C_{\beta,d},
+ \qquad |h|\le1,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+and the mean-value theorem gives \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \sqrt{1+|w+z|^2}
+ \le\sqrt{1+|w|^2}+|z|
+ \le(1+|z|)\sqrt{1+|w|^2},
+\]
+so
+\[
+ \log\frac{p_{\beta,d}(w)}{p_{\beta,d}(w+z)}
+ \le\beta\log(1+|z|).
+\]
+Integration against \(p_{\beta,d}(w)\dd w\) proves \textup{(K3)}.
+This supplies a nonstable polynomial-tail family for every \(\beta>d\);
+only the value \(\beta=d+1\) is the Poisson/stable case.
+
+\emph{Gaussian obstruction.}
+For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
+\[
+ \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
+ \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
+\]
+so the normalized derivatives are unbounded and \textup{(K1)} fails at its
+first derivative.  The translate quotient
+\[
+ F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
+\]
+has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\); hence the uniform lower bound for the
+actual quotients used by the two-background expansion is unavailable.  The
+proxy failure is already explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
+\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
+\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
+They have the same moments below order two.  For \(s>|m|+a\) the retained
+tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); therefore both
+prescribed proxies equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a half-line.
+Thus proxy positivity, the background lower bound, and the bounded cubic
+remainder all fail at the same additive-jet step.  Gaussian translate entropy
+itself is not the obstruction when \(r\ge2\), since
+\(\mathsf H_g(z)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments can and do prove
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input hypotheses,
+as recalled above, but they are not instances of this positive additive
+tail-proxy mechanism.
+\end{proof}

+\subsection*{The positive tail-jet mechanism for an abstract kernel}
+
+We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  Fix
+an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive probability density
+\(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet admissible of order \(r\)}
+if the following three conditions hold.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
+\]
+\item The top normalized derivative has the quotient translation modulus
+\[
+ \omega_{p,r}(t):=
+ \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
+                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
+ \qquad 0<t\le1,
+\]
+finite for \(0<t\le1\) and satisfying
+\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
+\item The translate entropy is finite and, for some \(C_{p,r}<\infty\),
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z):=
+ D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)
+ \le C_{p,r}(1+|z|^r),\qquad z\in\RR^d.
+\]
+\end{enumerate}
+Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
+\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
+\]
+For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
+\[
+ B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
+\]
+
+\begin{unnumberedtheorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
+Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
+probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
+\[
+ m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
+ \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
+\[
+ \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
+ V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
+ \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
+\begin{align*}
+ C_{p,r-1,s}
+ &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
+  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
+ A_{p,s}^\lambda
+ &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
+\end{align*}
+The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
+\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
+\[
+ k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
+\]
+are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
+\]
+is well defined.  If
+\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
+\[
+ B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
+ \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
+ \qquad
+ \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
+\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedtheorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We give every kernel-dependent step.  Let
+\[
+ \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
+ \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
+\]
+Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
+ +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
+ \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
+\]
+It also gives \(D^rp\in L^1\).  Consequently ordinary translation
+continuity in \(L^1\), the integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply
+that, for \(|z|\le1\),
+\begin{align*}
+ &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\\
+ &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
+\end{align*}
+where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
+zero.  Indeed, after subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial, the
+uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
+\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\[
+ |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
+ \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
+\]
+which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  This proves the required local Taylor statement
+without a derivative of order \(r+1\).
+
+Define the actual quotient
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
+the moments gives
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda
+ =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
+ +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+For completeness, after multiplication by \(s^r\) the interior Taylor
+remainder is dominated by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every
+discarded exterior mode satisfies
+\[
+ s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
+ \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad j\le r.
+\]
+The same tail-moment estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Translation preserves mass.  Hence \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\), and integration of
+the distributional derivatives of the integrable density \(p\) gives
+\(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass one,
+and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This is both proxy normalization and proxy positivity; no tail comparison is
+used.
+
+We next verify entropy finiteness.  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
+relative entropy and \textup{(K3)} give, for the normalized exterior mixture
+quotient \(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
+ \le\frac{C_{p,r}}{\tau_s^\lambda}
+ \int_{|x|>s}\{1+|x/s|^r\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The elementary inequalities
+\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
+\[
+ (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
+ \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
+\]
+then show
+\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
+The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
+common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.
+
+It remains to identify the quadratic term.  Condition \textup{(K1)} at
+order one says \(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty=L<\infty\).  Thus
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
+\]
+uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
+their common jet cancels, so
+\begin{align*}
+ \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
+ &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
+      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
+ \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
+ &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{align*}
+All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are now
+satisfied with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder
+calculation gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
+       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
+\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving the decomposition.
+
+Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
+vanishes, then
+\[
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p=0
+\]
+almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
+\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
+polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
+nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
+is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
+Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
+\end{proof}
+
+The hypotheses above are arranged by proof function, not by tail class.
+Condition \textup{(K1)} defines and bounds the retained modes, makes their
+integrals vanish, and supplies the logarithmic-gradient lower bound.
+Condition \textup{(K2)} is exactly the uniform little-\(o\) Taylor remainder;
+the \(L^1\) counterpart is automatic because \textup{(K1)} puts \(D^rp\) in
+\(L^1\).  Condition \textup{(K3)} is used only to make the retained-tail and
+proxy entropies finite.  Neither decay, regular variation, a semigroup law,
+radial symmetry, nor isotropy is assumed.  Isotropy merely adds orthogonal
+invariance of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\).
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Verified kernels and the Gaussian boundary]
+For every order \(r\ge1\), the abstract theorem applies to each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), to the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and to every multivariate Student kernel
+\[
+ p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
+\]
+For the stable density, the specialization is exactly Theorem
+\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, with identical
+proxies, energy, and quadratic form.  The standard Gaussian density is not
+tail-jet admissible: \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)} fail, and the additive
+retained common jet need not be positive.  Thus the abstract theorem makes no
+Gaussian claim.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+\emph{Isotropic stable kernels.}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} gives, with
+\(\beta=d+\alpha\),
+\[
+ p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
+ (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
+\]
+This proves \textup{(K1)}.  For \(|h|\le1\), the mean-value theorem, the
+bound at order \(r+1\), and
+\(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
+\[
+ \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
+ \le C|h|,qquad |\gamma|=r,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+so \textup{(K2)} holds.  The two-sided density estimate also gives
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z)\le C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|),
+\]
+which is \textup{(K3)} for every \(r\ge1\).  The abstract definitions of
+\(F_y^p\), \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\), \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are respectively the definitions used in
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Hence
+that theorem is precisely this specialization, not a weakened consequence.
+
+\emph{Poisson kernel.}
+At unit height the Poisson kernel on \(\RR^d\) is
+\[
+ P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}.
+\]
+The derivative calculation in the next paragraph with \(\beta=d+1\)
+verifies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}, while the displayed entropy bound
+there verifies \textup{(K3)}.  Its spatial dilates are exactly
+\(P_s^{(d)}(x)=c_ds(s^2+|x|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  This is also the
+\(\alpha=1\) stable member, but the rational formula proves membership
+directly, without stable-density estimates.
+
+\emph{Multivariate Student kernels.}
+Let \(\beta>d\).  Repeated differentiation shows that every normalized
+derivative \(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of
+terms
+\[
+ c_{\gamma,k}\,
+ \frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^{k}},
+ \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
+\]
+and is therefore bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together
+with
+\[
+ \frac{p_{\beta,d}(y-th)}{p_{\beta,d}(y)}\le C_{\beta,d},
+ \qquad |h|\le1,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+and the mean-value theorem gives \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \sqrt{1+|w+z|^2}
+ \le\sqrt{1+|w|^2}+|z|
+ \le(1+|z|)\sqrt{1+|w|^2},
+\]
+so
+\[
+ \log\frac{p_{\beta,d}(w)}{p_{\beta,d}(w+z)}
+ \le\beta\log(1+|z|).
+\]
+Integration against \(p_{\beta,d}(w)\dd w\) proves \textup{(K3)}.
+This supplies a nonstable polynomial-tail family for every \(\beta>d\);
+only the value \(\beta=d+1\) is the Poisson/stable case.
+
+\emph{Gaussian obstruction.}
+For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
+\[
+ \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
+ \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
+\]
+so the normalized derivatives are unbounded and \textup{(K1)} fails at its
+first derivative.  The translate quotient
+\[
+ F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
+\]
+has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\); hence the uniform lower bound for the
+actual quotients used by the two-background expansion is unavailable.  The
+proxy failure is already explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
+\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
+\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
+They have the same moments below order two.  For \(s>|m|+a\) the retained
+tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); therefore both
+prescribed proxies equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a half-line.
+Thus proxy positivity, the background lower bound, and the bounded cubic
+remainder all fail at the same additive-jet step.  Gaussian translate entropy
+itself is not the obstruction when \(r\ge2\), since
+\(\mathsf H_g(z)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments can and do prove
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input hypotheses,
+as recalled above, but they are not instances of this positive additive
+tail-proxy mechanism.
+\end{proof}

+The theorem is a specialization of the unnumbered abstract kernel theorem
+that precedes it.  For a strictly positive density \(p\), the proof uses only
+bounded normalized derivatives through order \(r\), uniform
+translation-continuity of the normalized order-\(r\) derivative, and an
+order-\(r\) bound on the entropy of a translate of \(p\).  These conditions
+hold for all isotropic strictly stable densities, for the Poisson kernel, and
+for every multivariate Student density \(c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2}\),
+\(\beta>d\).  No tail asymptotic or regular variation enters the abstract
+proof.  The Gaussian density does not satisfy the bounded normalized-jet
+condition: its normalized derivatives are Hermite polynomials, and an
+additive common jet need not remain positive.  Thus the Gaussian
+first-unmatched-moment theorem recalled above uses a different weighted
+Hermite mechanism; it is not presented as a member of the positive
+tail-proxy theorem.

+\subsection*{The positive tail-jet mechanism for an abstract kernel}
+
+We now separate the kernel properties from their stable implementation.  Fix
+an integer \(r\ge1\).  A strictly positive probability density
+\(p\in C^r(\RR^d)\) will be called \emph{tail-jet admissible of order \(r\)}
+if the following three conditions hold.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(K\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
+\item For every multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(1\le|\gamma|\le r\),
+\[
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty<\infty.
+\]
+\item The top normalized derivative has the quotient translation modulus
+\[
+ \omega_{p,r}(t):=
+ \max_{|\gamma|=r}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}
+ \left\|\frac{\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)
+                   -\partial^\gamma p}{p}\right\|_\infty,
+ \qquad 0<t\le1,
+\]
+finite for \(0<t\le1\) and satisfying
+\(\omega_{p,r}(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
+\item The translate entropy is finite and, for some \(C_{p,r}<\infty\),
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z):=
+ D_{\rm KL}\bigl(p(\mathord\cdot-z)\|p\bigr)
+ \le C_{p,r}(1+|z|^r),\qquad z\in\RR^d.
+\]
+\end{enumerate}
+Put \(p_s(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)\),
+\(\Omega_p(\dd y)=p(y)\dd y\), and
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)=\frac{p(y-z)}{p(y)}.
+\]
+For a law \(\lambda\) with finite \(r\)th absolute moment define
+\[
+ B_{p,j}^\lambda(y):=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{p(y)}
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=j}\frac{m_\gamma(\lambda)}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p(y),\qquad 1\le j\le r.
+\]
+
+\begin{unnumberedtheorem}[Abstract positive tail-jet kernel theorem]
+Let \(p\) be tail-jet admissible of order \(r\), and let \(\nu,\eta\) be
+probability laws on \(\RR^d\) such that
+\[
+ m_\gamma(\nu)=m_\gamma(\eta)\quad(|\gamma|<r),
+ \qquad \int |x|^r(\nu+\eta)(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+For \(\lambda\in\{\nu,\eta\}\), set
+\[
+ \tau_s^\lambda=\lambda(|x|>s),\qquad
+ V_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=
+ \int_{|x|>s}F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x),
+\]
+and let the common retained jet and the two proxies be
+\begin{align*}
+ C_{p,r-1,s}
+ &=\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\nu
+  =\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}B_{p,j}^\eta,\\
+ A_{p,s}^\lambda
+ &=1+C_{p,r-1,s}+V_{p,s}^\lambda-\tau_s^\lambda.
+\end{align*}
+The sum is empty when \(r=1\).  For all sufficiently large \(s\), both
+\(A_{p,s}^\lambda\) are positive probability densities relative to
+\(\Omega_p\).  Thus
+\[
+ k_{p,r,s}^\lambda(x)=s^{-d}p(x/s)A_{p,s}^\lambda(x/s)
+\]
+are probability densities and the finite, nonnegative proxy energy
+\[
+ \mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+ :=D_{\rm KL}(k_{p,r,s}^\nu\|k_{p,r,s}^\eta)
+\]
+is well defined.  If
+\(\Delta_r=\int x^{\otimes r}(\nu-\eta)(\dd x)\), put
+\[
+ B_{p,\Delta_r}(y)=
+ \frac{(-1)^r}{r!p(y)}\langle\Delta_r,D^rp(y)\rangle,
+ \qquad
+ \mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ =\frac12\int B_{p,\Delta_r}^2\dd\Omega_p.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)s^{-2r}
+  +\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+Moreover \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) is finite and positive definite on
+\(\operatorname{Sym}^r(\RR^d)\), and hence, law by law,
+\[
+ s^{2r}D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ \longrightarrow\mathcal Q_{p,r}(\Delta_r)
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
+ s^{2r}\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+\end{unnumberedtheorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+We give every kernel-dependent step.  Let
+\[
+ \mathsf B_{p,j}(y,z)=
+ \frac{(-1)^j}{j!p(y)}\langle D^jp(y),z^{\otimes j}\rangle,
+ \qquad \mathsf B_{p,0}=1.
+\]
+Condition \textup{(K1)} gives, for \(1\le j\le r\),
+\[
+ \|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_\infty
+ +\|\mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}
+ \le C_{p,r}|z|^j.
+\]
+It also gives \(D^rp\in L^1\).  Consequently ordinary translation
+continuity in \(L^1\), the integral Taylor formula, and \textup{(K2)} imply
+that, for \(|z|\le1\),
+\begin{align*}
+ &\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_\infty
+ +\left\|F_\cdot^p(z)-\sum_{j=0}^r
+       \mathsf B_{p,j}(\mathord\cdot,z)\right\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}\\
+ &\hspace{35mm}\le \varepsilon_{p,r}(|z|)|z|^r,
+\end{align*}
+where \(\varepsilon_{p,r}\) is bounded on \([0,1]\) and tends to zero at
+zero.  Indeed, after subtracting the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial, the
+uniform remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\(|z|^r\omega_{p,r}(|z|)\).  After multiplication by \(p(y)\), the
+\(L^1(\Omega_p)\) remainder is bounded by a constant times
+\[
+ |z|^r\max_{|\gamma|=r}\sup_{|h|\le|z|}
+ \|\partial^\gamma p(\mathord\cdot-h)-\partial^\gamma p\|_1,
+\]
+which is \(o(|z|^r)\).  This proves the required local Taylor statement
+without a derivative of order \(r+1\).
+
+Define the actual quotient
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)=\int F_y^p(x/s)\lambda(\dd x).
+\]
+Splitting at \(|x|=s\), retaining the exterior translate exactly, and using
+the moments gives
+\[
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda
+ =A_{p,s}^\lambda+s^{-r}B_{p,r}^\lambda+R_{p,s}^\lambda,
+ \qquad
+ \|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_\infty
+ +\|R_{p,s}^\lambda\|_{L^1(\Omega_p)}=o(s^{-r}).
+\]
+For completeness, after multiplication by \(s^r\) the interior Taylor
+remainder is dominated by \(C|x|^r\) and converges pointwise to zero.  Every
+discarded exterior mode satisfies
+\[
+ s^{-j}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^j\lambda(\dd x)
+ \le s^{-r}\int_{|x|>s}|x|^r\lambda(\dd x)=o(s^{-r}),
+ \qquad j\le r.
+\]
+The same tail-moment estimate gives \(\tau_s^\lambda=o(s^{-r})\).
+
+Translation preserves mass.  Hence \(V_{p,s}^\lambda\ge0\),
+\(\int V_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=\tau_s^\lambda\), and integration of
+the distributional derivatives of the integrable density \(p\) gives
+\(\int B_{p,j}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p=0\).  Therefore each proxy has mass one,
+and
+\[
+ \inf_yA_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge1-\|C_{p,r-1,s}\|_\infty-\tau_s^\lambda\longrightarrow1.
+\]
+This is both proxy normalization and proxy positivity; no tail comparison is
+used.
+
+We next verify entropy finiteness.  When \(\tau_s^\lambda>0\), convexity of
+relative entropy and \textup{(K3)} give, for the normalized exterior mixture
+quotient \(Q_{p,s}^\lambda=V_{p,s}^\lambda/\tau_s^\lambda\),
+\[
+ \int Q_{p,s}^\lambda\log Q_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p
+ \le\frac{C_{p,r}}{\tau_s^\lambda}
+ \int_{|x|>s}\{1+|x/s|^r\}\lambda(\dd x)<\infty.
+\]
+The elementary inequalities
+\(\Phi(\tau q)\le\tau q\log(1+q)\) for \(0\le\tau\le1\), and
+\[
+ (u+v)\log^+(u+v)\le C\{1+v+\Phi(v)\},
+ \qquad 0\le u\le3/2,\quad v\ge0,
+\]
+then show
+\(\int A_{p,s}^\lambda\log^+A_{p,s}^\lambda\dd\Omega_p<\infty\).
+The case \(\tau_s^\lambda=0\) is immediate.  Since the two proxies have a
+common positive lower bound, their relative entropy is finite.
+
+It remains to identify the quadratic term.  Condition \textup{(K1)} at
+order one says \(\|\nabla\log p\|_\infty=L<\infty\).  Thus
+\[
+ F_y^p(z)\ge e^{-L|z|},\qquad
+ q_{p,s}^\lambda(y)
+ \ge e^{-L\int|x|\lambda(\dd x)/s}\longrightarrow1
+\]
+uniformly in \(y\).  The backgrounds tend to one in \(L^1(\Omega_p)\), and
+their common jet cancels, so
+\begin{align*}
+ \|A_{p,s}^\lambda-1\|_1
+ &\le\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}s^{-j}\|B_{p,j}^\lambda\|_1
+      +2\tau_s^\lambda=o(1),\\
+ \|A_{p,s}^\nu-A_{p,s}^\eta\|_1
+ &\le2(\tau_s^\nu+\tau_s^\eta)=o(s^{-r}).
+\end{align*}
+All hypotheses of the two-background KL perturbation lemma are now
+satisfied with \(\epsilon_s=s^{-r}\).  Its Hessian and cubic-remainder
+calculation gives
+\[
+ D_{\rm KL}(p_s*\nu\|p_s*\eta)
+ =\mathcal E_{p,r,s}(\nu,\eta)
+  +\frac{s^{-2r}}2\int
+       (B_{p,r}^\nu-B_{p,r}^\eta)^2\dd\Omega_p+o(s^{-2r}).
+\]
+The moment identity makes the difference in the integral exactly
+\(B_{p,\Delta_r}\), proving the decomposition.
+
+Finiteness of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) follows from \textup{(K1)}.  If it
+vanishes, then
+\[
+ \sum_{|\gamma|=r}\frac{\Delta m_\gamma}{\gamma!}
+ \partial^\gamma p=0
+\]
+almost everywhere.  Fourier transformation gives
+\(P(i\xi)\widehat p(\xi)=0\), where \(P\) is the corresponding homogeneous
+polynomial.  Since \(\widehat p(0)=1\), continuity makes \(\widehat p\)
+nonzero on a neighborhood of zero.  Thus \(P\) vanishes on an open set and
+is identically zero.  Hence \(\Delta_r=0\), proving positive definiteness.
+Nonnegativity of the proxy KL energy proves the final equivalence.
+\end{proof}
+
+The hypotheses above are arranged by proof function, not by tail class.
+Condition \textup{(K1)} defines and bounds the retained modes, makes their
+integrals vanish, and supplies the logarithmic-gradient lower bound.
+Condition \textup{(K2)} is exactly the uniform little-\(o\) Taylor remainder;
+the \(L^1\) counterpart is automatic because \textup{(K1)} puts \(D^rp\) in
+\(L^1\).  Condition \textup{(K3)} is used only to make the retained-tail and
+proxy entropies finite.  Neither decay, regular variation, a semigroup law,
+radial symmetry, nor isotropy is assumed.  Isotropy merely adds orthogonal
+invariance of \(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\).
+
+\begin{unnumberedproposition}[Verified kernels and the Gaussian boundary]
+For every order \(r\ge1\), the abstract theorem applies to each isotropic
+strictly \(\alpha\)-stable density, \(0<\alpha<2\), to the Poisson kernel in
+every dimension, and to every multivariate Student kernel
+\[
+ p_{\beta,d}(y)=c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2},\qquad \beta>d.
+\]
+For the stable density, the specialization is exactly Theorem
+\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}, with identical
+proxies, energy, and quadratic form.  The standard Gaussian density is not
+tail-jet admissible: \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)} fail, and the additive
+retained common jet need not be positive.  Thus the abstract theorem makes no
+Gaussian claim.
+\end{unnumberedproposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+\emph{Isotropic stable kernels.}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package} gives, with
+\(\beta=d+\alpha\),
+\[
+ p(y)\asymp(1+|y|)^{-\beta},\qquad
+ |\partial^\gamma p(y)|\le C_\gamma
+ (1+|y|)^{-\beta-|\gamma|}.
+\]
+This proves \textup{(K1)}.  For \(|h|\le1\), the mean-value theorem, the
+bound at order \(r+1\), and
+\(1+|y|\le2(1+|y-th|)\) give
+\[
+ \frac{|\partial^\gamma p(y-h)-\partial^\gamma p(y)|}{p(y)}
+ \le C|h|,qquad |\gamma|=r,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+so \textup{(K2)} holds.  The two-sided density estimate also gives
+\[
+ \mathsf H_p(z)\le C+(d+\alpha)\log(1+|z|),
+\]
+which is \textup{(K3)} for every \(r\ge1\).  The abstract definitions of
+\(F_y^p\), \(B_{p,j}^\lambda\), \(A_{p,s}^\lambda\), and
+\(\mathcal Q_{p,r}\) are respectively the definitions used in
+Theorem~\ref{thm:stable-arbitrary-order-law-by-law-decomposition}.  Hence
+that theorem is precisely this specialization, not a weakened consequence.
+
+\emph{Poisson kernel.}
+At unit height the Poisson kernel on \(\RR^d\) is
+\[
+ P_1^{(d)}(y)=c_d(1+|y|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}.
+\]
+The derivative calculation in the next paragraph with \(\beta=d+1\)
+verifies \textup{(K1)} and \textup{(K2)}, while the displayed entropy bound
+there verifies \textup{(K3)}.  Its spatial dilates are exactly
+\(P_s^{(d)}(x)=c_ds(s^2+|x|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\).  This is also the
+\(\alpha=1\) stable member, but the rational formula proves membership
+directly, without stable-density estimates.
+
+\emph{Multivariate Student kernels.}
+Let \(\beta>d\).  Repeated differentiation shows that every normalized
+derivative \(\partial^\gamma p_{\beta,d}/p_{\beta,d}\) is a finite sum of
+terms
+\[
+ c_{\gamma,k}\,
+ \frac{y^{\delta_{\gamma,k}}}{(1+|y|^2)^{k}},
+ \qquad |\delta_{\gamma,k}|\le2k,
+\]
+and is therefore bounded.  The same statement one order higher, together
+with
+\[
+ \frac{p_{\beta,d}(y-th)}{p_{\beta,d}(y)}\le C_{\beta,d},
+ \qquad |h|\le1,quad0\le t\le1,
+\]
+and the mean-value theorem gives \(\omega_{p,r}(t)\le Ct\).  Finally,
+\[
+ \sqrt{1+|w+z|^2}
+ \le\sqrt{1+|w|^2}+|z|
+ \le(1+|z|)\sqrt{1+|w|^2},
+\]
+so
+\[
+ \log\frac{p_{\beta,d}(w)}{p_{\beta,d}(w+z)}
+ \le\beta\log(1+|z|).
+\]
+Integration against \(p_{\beta,d}(w)\dd w\) proves \textup{(K3)}.
+This supplies a nonstable polynomial-tail family for every \(\beta>d\);
+only the value \(\beta=d+1\) is the Poisson/stable case.
+
+\emph{Gaussian obstruction.}
+For the standard Gaussian \(g\),
+\[
+ \partial^\gamma g/g=(-1)^{|\gamma|}H_\gamma,
+ \qquad \nabla\log g(y)=-y,
+\]
+so the normalized derivatives are unbounded and \textup{(K1)} fails at its
+first derivative.  The translate quotient
+\[
+ F_y^g(z)=\exp\{y\mathbin\cdot z-|z|^2/2\}
+\]
+has infimum zero for every \(z\ne0\); hence the uniform lower bound for the
+actual quotients used by the two-background expansion is unavailable.  The
+proxy failure is already explicit in dimension one at \(r=2\).  Take
+\(\nu=\delta_m\) and
+\(\eta=(\delta_{m-a}+\delta_{m+a})/2\), where \(m\ne0\) and \(a>0\).
+They have the same moments below order two.  For \(s>|m|+a\) the retained
+tails vanish, while the common first Gaussian mode is \(my\); therefore both
+prescribed proxies equal \(1+my/s\), which is negative on a half-line.
+Thus proxy positivity, the background lower bound, and the bounded cubic
+remainder all fail at the same additive-jet step.  Gaussian translate entropy
+itself is not the obstruction when \(r\ge2\), since
+\(\mathsf H_g(z)=|z|^2/2\).  Weighted Hermite arguments can and do prove
+Gaussian first-unmatched-moment asymptotics under stronger input hypotheses,
+as recalled above, but they are not instances of this positive additive
+tail-proxy mechanism.
+\end{proof}

+The theorem is a specialization of the unnumbered abstract kernel theorem
+that precedes it.  For a strictly positive density \(p\), the proof uses only
+bounded normalized derivatives through order \(r\), uniform
+translation-continuity of the normalized order-\(r\) derivative, and an
+order-\(r\) bound on the entropy of a translate of \(p\).  These conditions
+hold for all isotropic strictly stable densities, for the Poisson kernel, and
+for every multivariate Student density \(c_{\beta,d}(1+|y|^2)^{-\beta/2}\),
+\(\beta>d\).  No tail asymptotic or regular variation enters the abstract
+proof.  The Gaussian density does not satisfy the bounded normalized-jet
+condition: its normalized derivatives are Hermite polynomials, and an
+additive common jet need not remain positive.  Thus the Gaussian
+first-unmatched-moment theorem recalled above uses a different weighted
+Hermite mechanism; it is not presented as a member of the positive
+tail-proxy theorem.

+\begin{lemma}[The two quadratic Pisot parameter chambers]

tools/chatgpt-oracle/sprint/ask/A3_tier_out.txt:3693: trailing whitespace.

tools/chatgpt-oracle/sprint/ask/A3_tier_out.txt:3694: trailing whitespace.

tools/chatgpt-oracle/sprint/ask/A3_tier_out.txt:3698: trailing whitespace.

+\]
tools/chatgpt-oracle/sprint/ask/A3_tier_out.txt:3703: trailing whitespace.

+\begin{proof}
tools/chatgpt-oracle/sprint/ask/A3_tier_out.txt:3712: trailing whitespace.
